title: Can wetlands cool the water footprint of AI data centers?
subtitle: Columbia University · Northern Virginia
summary: Northern Virginia is the world's largest data center cluster, and its facilities used about 1.85 billion gallons of water in 2023. This study asks whether nearby wetlands lower the heat that drives that water use, using satellite data and state water records.

keyResults.label: Wetlands run cooler in summer
keyResults.detail: Daytime surface temperature near Occoquan Bay wetland vs. Data Center Alley, 72 months (p < 0.001).

keyResults.label: Heat raises water use
keyResults.detail: Extra monthly groundwater withdrawal per +1 °C at one data center in the pilot model (p = 0.002).

keyResults.label: Cooling technology matters
keyResults.detail: Monthly drop in withdrawal after the facility's 2023 cooling retrofit (p < 0.001).
